environment: Apple M3, visible Chromium 157; production WebGL with luma 9.3.6 and candidate WebGPU with luma 10.0.0-alpha.15
scope: Karate Club: 34 points and 78 weighted links; selected timing, interaction and rendering checks with both viewers controlled by the test.
question: Can the experimental WebGPU viewer support a small graph exploration workflow?
method: Compare the production and WebGPU viewers on the same graph. Measure animation and interaction; separately compare their pixels with the same fixed point and link positions.
conclusion: Both viewers ran the small graph. The original comparison found differences on short links. A follow-up matched both frozen styles after applying production’s distance-based opacity.

checks.name: Evolving frame intervals
checks.detail: Both viewers met the 33 ms target in all 300 measured intervals.

checks.name: Point identities at fixed positions
checks.detail: Point identities matched away from edges; no invisible point IDs appeared in the picking image in the cooled style-A comparison.

checks.name: Colors · evolving geometry, style B
checks.detail: 707 interior color errors in 604,160 pixels, using the earlier comparator and its more conservative invisible-point boundary.

checks.name: Colors · fresh geometry, style A
checks.detail: 88 interior color errors in 604,160 pixels with the final comparator; maximum channel difference 35/255 against a 2/255 limit.

checks.name: Colors · fresh geometry, style B
checks.detail: 469 interior color errors in 604,160 pixels with the final comparator; maximum channel difference 56/255 against a 2/255 limit.

checks.name: Colors · distance opacity, frozen styles A and B
checks.detail: The 19 November replay matched all interior RGBA bytes in both styles on M3, testing 1,228,800 pixels per style.

checks.name: Full migration readiness
checks.detail: The small viewer does not cover the complete Cosmos API, features or devices.

limits: The color follow-up covers the two fresh styles at one camera on M3. The frame intervals measure display pacing. The earlier selection-latency outlier remains open.
visual: The live comparison above is a new local run. No image from the recorded run was retained here.
